author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing answers a page number below the first with the first page
summary: Asking the owner listing for a page numbered below the first is answered with the first page of owners rather than the error page. Today it is refused, which is the defect this slice fixes.
acceptance_criteria: given a request for the owner listing asking for page zero, when the listing is opened, then the first page of owners is listed and the request succeeds (HTTP 200)
given a request asking for a page numbered below zero, when the listing is opened, then the first page of owners is listed and the request succeeds (HTTP 200)
given a request asking for a page below the first, when the listing is opened, then the owners listed are the same ones the first page shows, and no error page is rendered
given a search by last name asking for a page below the first, when the listing is opened, then the first page of that search's matches is listed
non_goals: behavior for a page numbered beyond the last page
behavior for a page value that is not a number
changing how any other paged listing, including the veterinarian directory, handles out-of-range pages
notes: Bug report from the user: /owners?page=0 renders the error page. Root-cause triage belongs to system-design-expert; the requirement states only the expected behavior. Recorded in docs/prd.md under Owner records, with the current behavior as edge case 6 (known defect).

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Root cause: OwnerController.findPaginatedForOwnersLastName (line 133-137) converts the one-based request parameter to a zero-based index with `PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize)`. For page=0 the index is -1 and PageRequest.of rejects a negative index with IllegalArgumentException. No @ControllerAdvice or @ExceptionHandler exists anywhere in src/main/java, so the exception escapes to Spring Boot's default error dispatch and the error page renders. The fix needs no new pattern. The `page` query parameter is external input whose range is unvalidated; security-principles.md#trust-boundaries row 1 already requires validating range at the boundary, and its closing line places defensive checks at the boundary rather than in the core. That puts the clamp at the controller entry point, in processFindForm, not in the private pagination helper and not in OwnerRepository. processFindForm already normalizes its other external input in place (lastName null-to-empty and strip, lines 98-104); the page clamp joins that block. Clamping is request binding, not a business rule, so architecture-principles.md line 85 and validation-checklist line 144 are satisfied rather than strained. No docs/ writes were needed: system-design.md § Constants already records page size as an unlisted local, and adding a Known Defects row for a defect this slice removes would be immediately stale.
integration_points: All four acceptance criteria traverse the single processFindForm path; the last-name search criterion needs no separate change because the search text and the page number are consumed by the same method
The normalized page number feeds two consumers: findPaginatedForOwnersLastName (repository query) and addPaginationModel (the `currentPage` model attribute the ownersList template compares against)

patterns.description: In-method normalization of external request input already present in processFindForm: lastName is defaulted when null and stripped otherwise, before use. The page clamp is the same shape at the same boundary.

§ Trust Boundaries row 1 requires range validation of arriving request input before use; the section's closing line places the check at the boundary, not in the core. This is the architectural basis for clamping in the controller.

Web controller row: the controller binds the request, delegates, selects the response, and holds no business rule. Range normalization of a query parameter is binding, so this fix does not extend the open controller-rules deviation.
The file's existing @WebMvcTest(OwnerController.class) plus @MockitoBean OwnerRepository fixture and the george() factory are the harness the three new tests reuse.

risks.risk: Clamping inside findPaginatedForOwnersLastName only. The repository query would be correct but addPaginationModel would still publish currentPage=0, and the ownersList template keys its first/previous/next links and its page highlight off that value.
risks.mitigation: Normalize once at the top of processFindForm so a single value reaches both the repository call and addPaginationModel. Assert model attribute currentPage equals 1 to pin this.

risks.risk: Replacing the @RequestParam int page with Spring Data's Pageable argument resolver. That changes behavior for non-numeric and beyond-last page values, both declared non-goals, and rewrites the model contract the template reads.
risks.mitigation: Keep the @RequestParam(defaultValue = "1") int page signature and every existing model attribute name. The change is a clamp, nothing more.

risks.risk: Fixing VetController.findPaginated for symmetry. It carries the identical `PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize)` defect, and touching it breaches the third non-goal.
risks.mitigation: Leave /vets.html untouched. The vet-listing defect stays open for a future slice; extracting a shared pagination helper is the moment to consider when that slice lands, not now.

risks.risk: OwnerRepository is a Mockito stub in this test class, so a 200 and the ownersList view name alone do not prove the first page was requested. A clamp to any valid index would pass.
risks.mitigation: Assert the observable that encodes the requirement: currentPage equals 1, and capture the Pageable handed to findByLastNameStartingWith to assert getPageNumber() is 0. Do not assert PageRequest.of(0, 5) by equality, which would couple the test to the page size.

notes: Triage basis: direct source reads of OwnerController, OwnerRepository, VetController, ownersList.html, and OwnerControllerTests, plus a repository-wide grep for ControllerAdvice/ExceptionHandler/ErrorController (none found). No IntelliJ MCP oracle is connected in this run, so grep and file reads are the weaker basis and are labeled as such. The negative-index rejection in PageRequest.of could not be confirmed against a resolved jar (no dependency cache present on this host); it is the documented Spring Data contract and the arithmetic producing the negative index is directly readable at OwnerController:135. Containment: the fix touches one method in one controller and needs no change to the repository, the template, the message bundles, or any other paged listing. All three non-goals hold. Verdict is covered, not minor: no adjustment to a recorded pattern is required, and no docs/ file was written. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is a no-op. Testing notes for the implementer: testing-principles § Mocking Policy tolerates the class's existing mock-framework fixture, and reusing it beats introducing a second doubling mechanism into the same file; § Test Data Construction requires new tests to build owners through a factory, and george() already serves that role; the three test names in the prd-entry already satisfy the BDD naming school.

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: Class sweep for the finding class fixed here (unbounded numeric request parameter at the HTTP trust boundary reaching PageRequest.of). VetController.showVetList takes the same @RequestParam(defaultValue = "1") int page and passes it unclamped to PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize), so /vets.html?page=0 still throws IllegalArgumentException and renders the error page -- the identical defect REQ-OWN-005 fixes for /owners. The system-design Known Defects table records that the error page renders the exception message, so this path is the residual instance of the same information-disclosure surface (the leaked text is a Spring Data bounds message, no application or credential data, hence not blocking). The same class also has an upper end on both routes: a very large page (e.g. page=2000000000) makes the computed offset exceed the int range and reaches the error page too. Question for the PRD owner, not a change request on this slice: does the REQ-OWN-005 bar ("a page below the first is answered with the first page rather than refused") extend to the veterinarian listing and to pages above the last, or is REQ-OWN-005 deliberately scoped to /owners only? Deferring is legitimate; the point is that the decision be recorded rather than left implicit.

approved_aspects: Input validation at the trust boundary is total and allocation-free: Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) on a primitive int maps every value below 1 onto 1 with no unchecked branch, no exception path, and no arithmetic hazard -- clamped page - 1 cannot underflow, and Integer.MIN_VALUE (the usual negation-overflow trap for this pattern) is handled by construction because Math.max never negates.

Clamping happens once at the controller entry point and both downstream consumers (findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel) receive the clamped value, so no path can reach the repository or the model with the raw parameter. Passing the clamped value to addPaginationModel additionally removes a latent case where the model attribute currentPage could carry 0 or a negative number.

No new injection surface. The clamped value flows to a Spring Data PageRequest, never into query text; owner search continues through the parameterized derived query findByLastNameStartingWith, consistent with the SQL-injection row of the system-design threat model.

Template-injection check on the consuming view: owners/ownersList.html interpolates currentPage inside Thymeleaf preprocessing markers (@{'/owners?page=__${currentPage - 1}__'}), which substitutes into expression text before parsing. That construct would be an expression-injection hazard for a String, but currentPage is a primitive int bound by Spring MVC type conversion and now clamped, so only a numeric literal can reach the preprocessor. No user-controlled text is introduced into the rendered page by this change.

Information-disclosure posture improves rather than regresses: the change removes a reachable route to the error page, which per system-design Known Defects renders the exception message to the reader. One trigger of that surface is closed on /owners.

No hardcoded secrets or credential-adjacent material in the diff; the sweep over token/password/secret/key and the project's own credential vocabulary (datasource, url, username) returns nothing across all three changed files.

Supply chain unchanged: the change set touches no dependency manifest (no build.gradle, pom.xml, properties, or lockfile), so no new or upgraded coordinate enters the tree and the framework versions under review are unmoved by this diff. No CVE surface is added.

Tests exercise the boundary values that matter for the input-validation claim (page=0, page=-1, and the below-first page combined with a lastName search) and assert the zero-based index actually handed to the repository, which is the assertion that would catch a regression reopening the exception path.
